record.paper_title: Selection Principles in Mathematics: A Milestone of Open Problems
record.original_question: Let j be the least cardinal κ such that player ONE has a winning strategy in the game G1(K, D) on every Tychonoff space whose cellularity is at least κ, where K consists of open families whose members cover X and D consists of open families with dense union. Is j equal to any standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum?

evidence.quote: Let K denote the families U ∈ D such that {U : U ∈ U } is a cover of X.
Scheepers deﬁnes j as the minimal cardinal κ such that ONE has a winning strategy in G1(K, D) on each Tychonoﬀ space with cellularity at least κ, and shows that cov(M) ≤ j ≤ non(SM Z).
Problem 13.4 ([39, Problem 1]) . Is j equal to any standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be a Tychonoff topological space. The cellularity of $X$ is
$$c(X)=\sup\{|\mathcal A|:\mathcal A\text{ is a family of pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of }X\}+\aleph_0.$$

Let $\mathcal D$ denote the collection of families $\mathcal U$ of open subsets of $X$ whose union $\bigcup\mathcal U$ is dense in $X$, and let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal D$ denote the subcollection consisting of those families $\mathcal U$ such that $\{U:U\in\mathcal U\}$ is an open cover of $X$.

The game $G_1(\mathcal K,\mathcal D)$ on $X$ is played in $\omega$ innings. In inning $n\in\omega$, player ONE chooses $\mathcal U_n\in\mathcal K$ and then player TWO chooses $U_n\in\mathcal U_n$. Player TWO wins if $\{U_n:n\in\omega\}\in\mathcal D$, i.e. $\bigcup_{n\in\omega}U_n$ is dense in $X$; otherwise player ONE wins.

Define the cardinal
$$\mathfrak j=\min\{\kappa:\text{for every Tychonoff space }X\text{ with }c(X)\ge\kappa,\ \text{ONE has a winning strategy in }G_1(\mathcal K,\mathcal D)\text{ on }X\}.$$

It is known that $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal M)\le\mathfrak j\le\operatorname{non}(\mathrm{SMZ})$, where $\mathcal M$ is the ideal of meager subsets of the real line, $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal M)$ is the least cardinality of a covering of $\mathbb R$ by meager sets, $\mathrm{SMZ}$ denotes the class of strong measure zero subsets of $\mathbb R$, and $\operatorname{non}(\mathrm{SMZ})$ is the least cardinality of a subset of $\mathbb R$ that is not strong measure zero.

Problem. Is $\mathfrak j$ provably (in ZFC) equal to one of the standard cardinal characteristics of the continuum?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not return any source confirming that the cardinal $\mathfrak j$ defined via the game $G_1(\mathcal K,\mathcal D)$ on Tychonoff spaces of large cellularity has been identified with a standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum. Related game-theoretic cardinal bounds in this area continue to be studied (e.g., refinements of Scheepers–Tall type bounds), but no resolution of this specific identification question was located.

status_evidence.title: A definitive improvement of a game-theoretic bound and the long tightness game
status_evidence.snippet: Improves a game-theoretic cardinal bound of Scheepers and Tall using a long version of the Menger game.
status_evidence.claim: Work on game-theoretic cardinal bounds in selection-principles topology is ongoing, but this paper does not identify the cardinal j with a standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum.
